newsitem.title: India: India shares rally on renewed speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: India shares rally on renewed speculative buying.

text.p: ** (1300 GMT) - Stock prices finish with small gains
** Benchmark Bombay index up 1.47 pct to 3,427.09
** ITC rallies 4.6 pct at National Stock Exchange, up 1.3
pct at Bombay bourse on huge short-covering
** Calcutta index gains 6.42 pts to 443.93, National bourse
26.60 pts to 987.10, Madras falls 7.78 pts to 3,245.80
** Delhi stock index advances 3.72 pts to 720.90
** All bourses closed on Thursday for national holiday
Indian stocks ended in positive territory on Wednesday, boosted by speculative buying and short-covering in blue chip shares, traders said.
Action was focussed on tobacco conglomerate ITC, they said.
"The market was pushed up by speculative factors...heavy volumes in ITC shares," said chief dealer Sanjeev Choithani at Bombay brokerage Pashupati Advani.

The ITC stock notched up a gain of 5.50 rupees to end at 400.50 rupees at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). At the National Stock Exchange (NSE), ITC advanced 18.05 rupees, or 4.66 percent to 405.05 in volumes of 9.56 million shares.
Traders said an auction of shares, short-sold by market players, scheduled later on Wednesday by the NSE was the main factor driving the rally.
ITC headed the auction list with 682,800 shares, followed by SBI 54,750 shares and Reliance 53,200.
The BSE's top 30-share index hit the day's high of 3,464.58, but ended at 3,427.09 gaining 44.35 points, or 1.31 percent over Tuesday's close.
Dealers said foreign funds were moderate buyers in index-linked stocks, but local funds remained on the sidelines.
Top Indian financier Uday Kotak said on Wednesday he saw falling real interest rates driving up Indian stock markets.
"The way people will look at equities and real estate will change," Kotak, vice chairman of Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd told Reuters in an interview.
Reliance was up 11.70 rupees to 247.75, ACC 22.70 to 1,347.75, SBI 2.0 to 277.0, TISCO 4.0 to 190.25, BSES 5.50 to 221.25, MTNL 3.0 to 242.0 and Ranbaxy 6.25 to 603.25.
Banks and stock exchanges across India, including the BSE and the NSE, are closed on January 23 for a national holiday.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
